title: Fair Contracts in Principal-Agent Games with Heterogeneous Types
abstract: arXiv:2506.15887v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Fairness is desirable yet challenging to achieve within multi-agent systems, especially when agents differ in latent traits that affect their abilities. This hidden heterogeneity often leads to unequal distributions of wealth, even when agents operate under the same rules. Motivated by real-world examples, we propose a framework based on repeated principal-agent games, where a principal, who also can be seen as a player of the game, learns to offer adaptive contracts to agents. By leveraging a simple yet powerful contract structure, we show that a fairness-aware principal can learn homogeneous linear contracts that equalize outcomes across agents in a sequential social dilemma. Importantly, this fairness does not come at the cost of efficiency: our results demonstrate that it is possible to promote equity and stability in the system while preserving overall performance.

translated_title: 具有异质类型的委托-代理博弈中的公平合同
translated_abstract: 公平性在多智能体系统中是人们期望实现却颇具挑战的目标，尤其是当智能体在影响其能力的潜在特质上存在差异时。这种隐藏的异质性往往导致财富分配不均，即使所有智能体都在相同的规则下运行。受现实世界案例的启发，我们提出了一个基于重复委托-代理博弈的框架，其中委托人（同时也可视为博弈中的一个参与者）学会向智能体提供自适应的合同。通过利用一个简单而强大的合同结构，我们证明了具有公平意识的委托人可以学习到同质的线性合同，从而在序贯社会困境中使各智能体之间的结果趋于均等。重要的是，这种公平性并不以牺牲效率为代价：我们的结果表明，在保持整体性能的同时，促进系统的公平性与稳定性是可行的。
tldr: 该论文提出基于重复委托-代理博弈的公平合同框架，证明具有公平意识的委托人可以通过学习同质线性合同，在不牺牲整体效率的前提下实现异质智能体间结果的均等化，兼顾公平与稳定。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a fairness-aware framework in repeated principal-agent games, showing that a principal can learn homogeneous linear contracts to equalize outcomes across heterogeneous agents while preserving overall efficiency and stability.
